0.en: [Basic Conception for the Spirit of Christianity]

en: 95) At the time when Jesus appeared among the Jewish nation, it found itself in the condition that is the condition of a revolution occurring sooner or later and that always bears the same general characters.

When the spirit has departed out of a constitution, out of the laws, and the former through its change no longer agrees with these, there arises a seeking, a striving after something else, which is soon found by each in something else, whereby then a manifoldness of formations, of ways of life, of claims, of needs emerges, which, when they gradually diverge so far that they can no longer exist side by side, finally bring about an outbreak and give their determinate being to a new general form, a new bond of human beings; the looser this bond is, the more it leaves ununited, the more seed of new inequalities and future explosions lies in it.
zh: 95) 耶稣在犹太民族中出场的时候，这个民族正处在那样一种状态中，那种状态是一场或早或晚要发生的革命的条件，并且总是带着同样的那些普遍特征。

当精神已经离开一种宪法、离开法律，而精神又通过自身的变化不再与这些法律相合时，就产生出一种寻找，一种对别的东西的追求，这种东西很快就被每个人在某种别的东西中找到，由此便出现形态、生活方式、要求、需要的杂多，这些杂多如果渐渐分叉到再也不能并立的地步，终于会引发一次爆发，并给一种新的普遍形式、一条人与人之间的新纽带以它们的定在；这条纽带越松，它让人不能结合的地方越多，其中就有越多的种子，长出新的不平等和未来的爆炸。

en: Thus the Jewish people at the time of Jesus no longer gives us the picture of a whole; a universal still holds it together in a makeshift way, but there is so much alien and manifold material, so many kinds of life and ideals, so much unsatisfied striving, looking about curiously for something new, that every reformer appearing with confidence and hopes can consider himself as assured of a following as of a hostile party.
zh: 所以耶稣那个时代的犹太民族给我们的已经不再是一个整体的图像；一种普遍的东西还勉强把他们维系在一起，但现成摆着的是那么多异质的、杂多的材料，那么多各式各样的生活和理想，那么多不满足的、好奇地四处张望新东西的追求，以至于每一个带着信心和希望出场的改革者，都可以同样有把握地认为自己有一批追随者，也照样有把握地认为自己有一个敌对的党。

en: The external independence of the Jewish state was lost; the Romans and the kings tolerated or given by the Romans therefore fairly united the general secret hatred of the Jews against themselves; the demand for independence lay too deep in their religion, which scarcely granted other peoples even to exist alongside it; how should it find the rule of one of these over its children tolerable?

The people, whose other actuality still remained uninjured, was not yet at the point of having to want to sacrifice this, and therefore waited for a foreign Messiah equipped with power, who would do for it what it itself did not dare, or inspired it to dare and swept it along through this violence.
zh: 犹太国家的外部独立已经失去，罗马人以及罗马人所容忍的或扶立的国王，因此把犹太人普遍而隐秘的仇恨相当一致地引到自己身上；对独立的要求太深地扎根在他们的宗教里，这种宗教几乎不肯让别的民族在它旁边存在；它怎么能受得了这些民族中的一个来统治自己的孩子呢？
这个民族其余的的现实性还没有受到损伤，它还没有到非牺牲这些不可的地步，所以它等待一个外来的、配备了权力的弥赛亚，由他来替它做它自己不敢做的事，或者把它鼓动起来去敢做，并凭借这种强力把它卷走。

en: Many distinguished themselves through a stricter and more exact observance of all religious punctilios, and the very fact that they distinguished themselves by this shows us the loss of unconstraint, the effort and a struggle to attain something that did not come forth out of itself.

The service in which they stood was the service toward a blind fate, not (like the Greek one) a fate lying within nature, and their greater religiosity [was] a more constant clinging to and dependence on something more manifold, which would relate to the One, but excluded every other consciousness.
The Pharisees sought with effort to be perfect Jews, and this proves that they knew the possibility of not being so.

The Sadducees let their Jewish element subsist in them as something actual, because it was once there, and were content with little, but it seemed to have no interest for them immediately except only insofar as it was once the condition of their remaining enjoyment; otherwise they and their determinate being were to themselves the highest law.
The Essenes too did not enter into a struggle with it, but let it lie aside, for in order to escape the strife they threw themselves into their monotonous way of life.
zh: 许多人靠更严格、更精确地遵守一切宗教上的细微末节而显得突出，而他们正由此显得突出，这本身就向我们表明无拘无束状态的丧失，表明那种辛苦和一场斗争，为的是达到某种不是从自身产生出来的东西。
他们所身处的侍奉，是对一种盲目的命运的侍奉，这种命运并不（像希腊人的命运那样）落在自然之内，而他们更强的宗教性［是］一种更持久地依恋和依赖于更杂多的东西，这些东西会关联到那唯一者，却把任何别的意识都排除在外。
法利赛人费尽气力想成为完全的犹太人，而这恰好证明，他们知道有可能不是这样的人。
撒都该人则把他们那点犹太的东西作为一种现实的东西留在自身之内，因为它已经在那里了，他们满足于很少的东西，但对他们来说，它直接看来只有作为他们其余享受的条件才有意义，除此以外，他们和他们的定在对他们自己就是最高的法律。
艾赛尼派也不与它进入斗争，而是把它搁在一边，因为他们为了逃避这场争执，就投身于他们那种单调一律的生活方式。

en: Finally someone had to appear who directly attacked Judaism itself; but because he did not find in the Jews that which would have helped him to contest it, that which he could have held fast to and with which he could have overthrown it, he had to perish and to have immediately founded only a sect.
zh: 最后必定要有一个人出场，直接攻击犹太教本身；但因为他没能在犹太人身上找到那种能帮他驳倒犹太教的东西，那种他能抓住、并借以把犹太教推翻的东西，所以他必定要毁灭，而且必定直接只创立了一个教派。

en: The root of Judaism is the objective, i.e. the service, the bondage of a foreign being.
This Jesus attacked.
zh: 犹太教的根是客观的东西，也就是侍奉，是受一个外来者的奴役。
耶稣攻击的就是这一点。

en: a) Bondage to their law, the will of the Lord - opposed to it, self-determination, self-activity.
What is bondage to a law?
zh: a) 对他们的法律、即主的意志的奴役——与之相对的是自我规定、自我活动。
对一条法律的奴役是什么？

en: α) in the opposed - will-lessness; β) in relation to other human beings - feelinglessness, lack of beautiful relations, love, separation γ) godlessness
zh: α) 在对立的一面——无意志；β) 在与别人的关系上——无情感，缺少美好的关系，爱，分离 γ) 无神

en: b) The Lord, the invisible Lord - opposed to him, fate-lessness, either of innocence or of self-power; the former not possible, he could not unite the two opposites in it, because properly only one of the opposites ruled without conflict, - the latter not, as godlessness - thus the dominion softened into fatherhood - dependence on one who loves with regard to need.
zh: b) 主，不可见的主——与之相对的是无命运，或者属于无辜的无命运，或者属于自身力量的无命运；前一种不可能，他无法把两个对立的东西结合到它里面，因为实际上只有对立双方中的一个在毫无冲突地统治着，——后一种不可能，那是无神——所以统治被缓和为父性——在困厄中依赖一个爱着的人。

en: c) Others determined α) either by me - opposed to this, morality, or β) by another (contempt for human beings, egoism and hoping for objective help) - respect of others, correction or annihilation of this hope.
Authority against authority - solely on the authority of faith in human nature.
John: he knew what power was in the human being.
Miracles - he also hoped for their effect - something real, not polemical.
The stirring up of the subjective in various respects - to found a beautiful religion, the ideal of it? does one find it?
zh: c) 他人被规定，α) 或者由我规定——与此相对的是道德，或者 β) 由另一个规定（对人的蔑视、利己主义和对客观帮助的指望）——对他人的尊重，对这种指望的纠正或消灭。
权威对权威——只依靠对人性之信仰的权威。
约翰（Joh[annes]）：他知道人里面有什么样的力量。
奇迹——他也指望过奇迹的作用——是实在的东西，不是论战的东西。
在种种方面把主观的东西鼓动起来——要创立一种美的宗教，它的理想？找得到吗？

en: Only then can a distinction be made between ceremonial and moral laws, when morality is claimed; in the Jewish religion morality [is] impossible, because there was no freedom in it, but thoroughgoing dominion.
zh: 只有在道德被归给人的时候，才能区分仪式的法律和道德的法律；在犹太宗教里道德不可能，因为其中没有自由，只有贯穿一切的统治。

en: In general [Jesus set] the subject against the law.
zh: 一般说来，[耶稣把]主体放到了法律的对面。

en: To the law he opposed morality? - morality is, according to Kant, the subjugation of the individual under the universal, the victory of the universal over its opposite, the individual - rather the elevation of the individual to the universal, union - sublation of the two opposites through union.
zh: 与法律相对，他放上的是道德？——按照康德，道德是把单个的东西压在普遍的东西之下的压制，是普遍的东西对与它相对立的单个的东西的胜利——不如说是单个的东西向普遍的东西的提升，是结合——通过结合来扬弃两个对立的东西。

en: a) Unity in the determinate presupposes freedom, for a limited thing has an opposite96)
zh: a) 在确定的东西之中的统一以自由为前提，因为一个受限制的东西有一个与它对立的东西96)

en: b) Unity of the whole human being
zh: b) 整个人的统一

en: c) The ideal of unity.
zh: c) 统一的理想。

en: The idea of their will is the opposite of the will; its purpose [is] not to will; but the object of the action, the thought, the purpose [is] always a drive, an activity, namely a reflected one, but not of the passive human being, thus of a foreign will; for a determinate action a determinate will, drive [is] necessary; but this determinate will [is] not actual in the passive human being, thus only in the idea, in the representation.
This foreign will [is] an objective law.
zh: 他们意志的观念是意志的反面；它的目的〔是〕不意愿；但行动的对象、思想、目的〔是〕始终是一种冲动、一种活动，也就是一种被反思过的冲动和活动，不过不是被动的人的，而是一个异己意志的；对一定的行动来说，一定的意志、冲动是必要的；可这个一定的意志在被动的人那里并不现实，所以只存在于观念中，存在于表象中。
这个异己的意志〔是〕一条客观的法则。

en: In that he showed them they have a bad will, he showed them they have a will.
zh: 他向他们指出他们有一个坏的意志，也就向他们指出他们有一个意志。

en: In the Sermon on the Mount, always a setting-over-against of the objective commandment and of duty; a sacrifice not, say, in order that something be given and forgiven, but you shall forgive; — an oath not holy on account of the temple, but you shall be truthful; the action and your intention shall be one, you shall perform the action in its whole extent, every action stems from a law, this law shall also be your own.
zh: 在登山宝训里，总是把客观的诫命和义务摆到对面；献祭并不是为了借此让什么被赠予、被宽恕，而是你们应当宽恕；——起誓并不因为圣殿才是神圣的，而是你们应当真诚；行动和你们的意图应当是一回事，你们应当把行动在其全部范围内做完，每一个行动都出自一条法则，这条法则也应当是你们自己的。

en: Of the moral commandments only the prohibitions are capable of becoming objective; moral commandments are unions expressed as rules, rules are the relations of objects to one another; the external relation, i.e. the relation of separated ones, can be stated only negatively, i.e. as a prohibition; for the living union, unity in the moral action is no external one, i.e. the related ones are no longer separated ones.
zh: 在道德的诫命中，只有禁令能够成为客观的；道德的诫命是被当作规则表达出来的结合，规则是各个对象彼此之间的关系；外在的关系，也就是分离者的关系，只能是否定地、也就是作为禁令被说出来；因为道德行动里那活生生的结合、那统一不是外在的，也就是说，被关联起来的双方不再是分离的。

en: Morality is the sublation of a separation in life, theoretical unity is unity of opposites — the principle of morality is love; relation in separation: determining or being determined, the former immoral toward others, the latter toward oneself — for both are only the producing of a theoretical unity.
Willing is the excluding of the opposite — the deed is the sublating of the separation between the willed, still now represented, and the striving, the activity, the drive, the willing one.

With a positive law the action is no union, but a being determined; the principle not love; the motive is a moving ground in the proper sense, it behaves as cause, as effecting; it is something foreign, not a modification of the willing one.
The object of the action in the positive is not the reflected drive itself or the drive as object, but something foreign, something different from the drive.
zh: 道德是对生命中一种分离的扬弃，理论的统一是对立者的统一——道德的原则是爱；分离中的关系：规定或被规定，前者对别人是不道德的，后者对自己是不道德的——因为两者都只是造成一种理论的统一。
意愿就是排斥那对立的东西，——行为则是扬弃被意愿的、现在还被表象的东西与努力、活动、冲动、意愿者之间的分离。
在一条实证的法则那里，行动不是结合，而是一种被规定；原则不是爱；动机是本义上的动因，它作为原因、作为起作用者出现；它是一个异己的东西，而不是意愿者的一种改变。
在实证的东西那里，行动的对象不是被反思过的冲动本身，也不是作为对象的冲动，而是一个异己的东西，一个与冲动不同的东西。

en: Kant's practical reason is the capacity of universality, i.e. the capacity to exclude; the motive [is] respect; this excluded thing subjugated in fear — a disorganization, the excluding of something still united; the excluded is not a sublated thing, but a separated one still subsisting.

The commandment is indeed subjective, a law of the human being, but a law that contradicts the other things present in him, a law that rules, it only commands, respect drives to action, but respect is the opposite of the principle according to which the action is; the principle is universality; respect is not this; the commandments are for respect always something given.
zh: 康德的实践理性是普遍性的能力，也就是排斥的能力；动力〔是〕敬重；这被排斥的东西在恐惧中被压服——一种解体，对某个还结合在一起的东西的排斥；被排斥的东西不是被扬弃了的东西，而是一个仍然存在的、被分离的东西。
诫命固然是主观的，是人的一条法则，但这是一条与人身中其他现存的东西相矛盾的法则，一条进行统治的法则，它只是下命令，敬重驱使人去行动，可敬重是同行动所遵循的那条原则相反的；原则是普遍性；敬重不是这个；对敬重来说，那些诫命永远是一种被给予的东西。

en: Jesus sets disposition over against the commandment, i.e. the inclination to act thus; inclination is grounded in itself, has its ideal object in itself; not in something foreign (the moral law of reason).

He does not say: keep such commandments because they are commandments of your spirit, not because they were given to your forefathers, but because you yourselves give them to yourselves — thus he does not say; he sets the disposition over against them, the inclination to act morally.

Since a moral action is limited, the whole from which it comes is also always limited and shows itself only in this limitation; but it is determined only by its object, by the particular kind of separation that it sublates; otherwise, within this boundary, its principle is complete union; but since this disposition is conditioned, is limited, it rests and acts only when the condition enters, then it unites; so it is on the one hand visible only in acting, in what it does (one cannot say of it in the full sense: it is, because it is not unconditional), on the other hand it is not completely presented in the action.

For the action shows only the effected objective relation of those present in the action; not the union that is the living thing; but because this union is only in this action, it stands single and isolated; no more has been united than has happened in this action.
zh: 耶稣把意向摆到诫命的对面，也就是这样行动的倾向；偏好是建立在自身之中的，它的理想对象就在它自己里面；而不是在一个异己的东西里（在理性的道德法则里）。
他没有说：要遵守这样的诫命，因为它们是你们精神的诫命，不是因为它们曾被给予你们的祖先，而是因为你们自己把它们给予自己——他没有这样说；他摆到对面的是意向，是道德地行动的倾向。

既然一种道德行动是受限制的，那么它由之而来的那个整体也始终是受限制的，并且只在这种限制中显露出来；可它只是通过它的对象、通过它所扬弃的那种特殊的分离方式才被规定的；除此以外，在这条界限之内，它的原则就是完整的结合；但既然这种意向是有条件的、是受限制的，它就静止着，只有在条件出现时才行动，这时它才去结合；所以它一方面只在行动中、在它所做的事情中才看得见（人们不能在完全的意义上说：它是，因为它不是无条件的），另一方面它在行动中并没有被完整地表达出来。
因为行动只显示出在行动中现存的那些东西之间被造成了的客观关系；而不是那活生生的结合；但因为这种结合只在这一行动中，它就单个地、孤立地立着；被结合起来的东西并没有比在这一行动中发生的更多。

en: If at the same time there is a striving present to multiply these acts, then the principle is no longer a resting disposition; a need is present, and the need of a whole of union, the need of love (general human love); it seeks to create the whole in an infinite manifoldness of actions, to give to the limitedness of the single action, through the multitude and the multiplication, the illusion of the whole, of the infinite.

Therefore beautiful souls who are unhappy, either because they are conscious of their fate or because they are simply not satisfied in the whole fullness of their love, are so beneficent — they have beautiful moments of enjoyment, but also only moments, and the tears of pity, of emotion over such a beautiful action are melancholy over its limitedness — or the stubborn rejection of the acceptance of thanks, the hidden magnanimity [is] a shame over the defectiveness of the condition.
The benefactor is always greater than the receiver.
zh: 如果同时还有一种把这些行为繁殖增多的追求，那么原则就不再是一种静止的意向；这里有一种需要，而且是结合之整体的需要，是爱的需要（普遍的人类之爱）；它要在无限杂多的行动中把整体创造出来，要通过数量和繁殖增多，给单个行动的受限制之处造出那整体、那无限者的假象。
所以，那些不幸福的美好灵魂——或者是因为它们意识到自己的命运，或者只是因为它们没有在自己爱的全部充实中得到满足——才那样乐善好施；它们有享受的美好环节，但也只是环节，而面对这样一种美好行动所流的同情之泪、感动之泪，是对它的受限制状态的伤感——或者，那种固执地拒绝接受感谢、那种隐藏的大度〔是〕对状态之缺陷的羞耻。
施惠的人总是比受惠的人更大。

en: In [the Gospels of] Matthew, Mark and Luke Christ [is] more in opposition to the Jews — more morality.

In John [the Gospel, he is] more himself, of more religious content, his relation to God and his congregation, his unity with the Father, and how his followers shall be one with him and among themselves — he the centre and the head; as in the most living union of several human beings a separation still always takes place, so also in this union — this the law of humanity; in the ideal that is fully united which is still separated, the Greeks in national gods, the Christians in Christ.
zh: 在马太、马可和路加〔的福音书〕里，基督更多地处在同犹太人的对立中——更多的是道德。
在约翰〔福音书里〕他更多的是他自己，更多的是宗教内容，是他对上帝、对他的教团的关系，是他同父的统一，以及他的追随者应当怎样同他、并在彼此之间成为一——他是中心、是头；正如在许多人最活生生的结合中总还是有一种分离发生，在这种结合里也一样——这就是人类的法则；在理想中，那还分离着的东西被完全结合起来了，希腊人在民族神里，基督徒在基督里。

en: a) Morality
zh: a) 道德

en: b) Love
zh: b) 爱

en: c) Religion — I, Christ — the kingdom of God — its shape under these circumstances — miracle.
zh: c) 宗教——我、基督——上帝之国——它在这种情况下的形态——奇迹。

en: Disposition sublates the positivity, the objectivity of the commandments; love the limits of disposition, religion the limits of love. —
zh: 意向扬弃诫命的实证性、客观性；爱扬弃意向的界限，宗教扬弃爱的界限。——

en: In objective human beings he [sc. man] is opposed to the power that rules him, and to that extent he is passive; insofar as he is active, he behaves just the same, there is a passive [being] over against him; he is always a slave as against a tyrant and at the same time a tyrant as against slaves; in a positive religion [is] man on the one hand determined, ruled, God the ruler, — even his opposite [is] as something objective not alone, not lonely; also something ruled by God.

Through disposition only the objective law is sublated, but not the objective world; man stands singly, and the world. — Love ties points together in moments, but the world in it, man and their domination still persists.

The domination of the Jews [is] different from tyranny, because the tyrant is something actual, their Jehovah something invisible; the actual tyrant is hostile, the tyrannical idea at the same time protective; for everyone is the darling of his idea — the ruling idea rules me, is against me; but at the same time, in my opposition to the world, it is on my side.97)
zh: 在客观的人那里，他[即人]与统治他的力量相对立，就此而言他是受动的；就他是行动的而言，他的情形也一样，他面前有一个受动的东西；他总是面对暴君的奴隶，同时又是面对奴隶的暴君；在实证宗教里，人一方面是被规定的、被统治的，上帝是统治者——他那对立面作为客观的东西也不是单独的、孤单的；也是受上帝统治的东西。
通过意向，被扬弃的只是客观的法则，而不是客观的世界；人个别地站着，世界也如此。——爱在一些环节中把点连结起来，但爱之中的世界、人以及它们的统治仍然存在。
犹太人所受的统治与暴政不同，因为暴君是现实的东西，他们的耶和华却是看不见的东西；现实的暴君是敌对的，暴虐的观念同时又是保护的；因为每个人都是自己观念的宠儿——统治的观念统治着我，与我作对；但同时在我对世界的对立中，它站在我这边。97)

en: With the objective law a part of ruling and of being ruled falls away; a law is an activity as effect, thus a determinate, limited activity that is an effect when a condition enters — or rather the connection itself between the condition and the activity as effect; if the connection is necessary, [there is] a must; if the non-externalization of the activity is possible, an ought.
If the connection is necessary, [there is] no freedom; this in two ways: the complete ground, i.e. the complete connection, in the condition itself, — living effect, or not in the condition, — dead.
Between the two, freedom and laws.
zh: 随着客观法则，一部分统治和被统治消失了；一条法则是一种作为效果的活动，也就是一种确定的、有限的活动，它在某个条件出现时是一种效果——或者更确切地说，是条件与作为效果的活动之间的联系本身；这联系如果是必然的，就是一种必须；如果这种活动可以不表露出来，就是一种应当。
如果这联系是必然的，就没有自由；这有两种情形：完整的根据，也就是完整的联系，在条件本身之中——活的效果，或者不在条件之中——死的。
两者之间是自由和法则。

en: a) Fitness for combating the objective.
zh: a) 与客观的东西作斗争的能力。

en: b) Deficiency.
zh: b) 缺陷。

en: Morality sublates only the being-ruled of the I and with it its ruling over living beings; but through this the living is still a multitude of absolutely separated, unconnected [beings], and an infinite dead material still remains over — and these isolated ones still need a ruler, a God, and the moral being itself [needs] a ruler insofar as it is not moral (not: immoral).

It is something resting that does no violence and suffers none; [that] also, where violence is done to a being by a third, remedies it; the universality is a dead one, for it is opposed to the individual, and life is the union of both, — morality is dependence on myself, disunion within itself.
zh: 道德只扬弃了自我被统治的状态，从而也扬弃了它对活的东西的统治；但这样一来，活的东西仍然是一堆绝对分离的、没有联系的东西，还剩下无限的死材料——而这些孤立者仍然需要一个统治者、一个上帝，道德的存在者本身只要不是道德的（不是：不道德的），也就需要一个统治者。
它是一种静止的东西，不施加暴力，也不遭受暴力；[它]在某个存在者受到第三者暴力对待时也会去补救；这种普遍性是死的，因为它与个别者相对立，而生命是两者的结合——道德则是对我自己的依赖，是自身之内的分裂。

en: The moral law at the same time sublates the purely positive commandments, in that it recognizes no law as its own, but [is] inconsistent in this, in that it is not merely something determining but something determinable; thus it still stands under a foreign power.
zh: 道德法则同时扬弃了纯粹实证的诫命，因为它不承认任何法则为自己的法则，但在这里并不一贯，因为它毕竟不只是规定着的东西，而且是可被规定的东西；所以它仍然处在外来力量之下。

en: With the change of the objective law the other sides of the Jew's relation had also to change.

If man himself has will, then he stands in a wholly different relation to God than the merely passive man; two independent wills, two substances, do not exist; God and man must therefore be — but man the son and God the father; man not independent and subsisting on himself, he is only insofar as he is opposed, is a modification, and therefore the father is also in him; in this son his disciples are also [present]; they too are one with him; a real transubstantiation, a real indwelling of the father in the son and of the son in his pupils — these all [are] not substances, absolutely separated and united only in the general concept, but like a vine and its branches; a living life of the Godhead in them. — This faith in him Jesus demands, — faith in the son of man; that the father dwells in him, and whoever believes in him, in him he too and the father dwell also.

This faith is immediately opposed to the objectivity of passivity and distinguishes itself from the passivity of the enthusiasts, who want to produce or feel a dwelling of God and Christ in themselves, in that they here distinguish themselves and this being ruling in them, and are thus again those ruled by an object; and to want to free us from an objective historical Christ and from dependence on him by making him so subjective that he is an ideal means precisely to take his life from him, to make him a thought, over against man a substance — and a thought is not the living God.

To make him a mere teacher of men means to take the Godhead out of the world, nature and man. — Jesus called himself the Messiah; a son of man and no other could be it, only unbelief in nature could expect another, a supernatural one; — the supernatural is present only with the sub-natural; for the whole, although separated, must always be there. — God is love, love is God, there is no other Godhead than love — only what is not divine, what does not love, must have the Godhead in the idea, outside itself.
Whoever cannot believe that God was in Jesus, that he dwells in men, despises men.

If love dwells, if God dwells among men, then there can be gods; where not, then one must speak of him, and no gods are possible; the gods are only the ideals of the individual separations; if everything is separated, then there is only one ideal.
zh: 随着客观法则的改变，犹太人所处关系的其他方面也必然改变。

人自己如果有意志，他与上帝的关系就和仅仅被动的人完全不同；两个独立的意志、两个实体是不存在的；所以上帝和人必须存在——但人是儿子，上帝是父亲；人不是独立的、不是自立的，他只是作为被对立起来的东西、作为一种样式才存在，因此父亲也在他之中；在这个儿子里也有他的门徒；他们与他同样是一体的；这是一种现实的实体转化，是父亲在儿子之中、儿子在他的学生之中的现实内住——所有这些[都]不是实体，不是绝对分离、只在一般概念中才联合起来的东西，而像一株葡萄藤和它的枝条；是神性在他们之中的活生生的生命。——耶稣要求的就是对他的这种信仰——对人之子的信仰；相信父亲住在他之中，而谁信他，他和父亲也住在谁之中。
这种信仰直接与被动状态的客观性相对立，并且不同于狂热者的被动状态，这些人想在自身中产生或感受到上帝和基督的内住，因为他们在这里把自己同那个在他们之中统治的存在者区分开来，于是又成了被一个对象统治的人；而想通过把基督弄得如此主观、以至于他成了一个理想，来把我们从客观的历史的基督以及对它的依赖中解放出来，这恰恰意味着夺去他的生命，把他变成一个思想，在人面前变成实体——而一个思想并不是活的上帝。
把他变成仅仅做人的教师，就意味着把神性从世界、自然和人那里拿走。——耶稣自称弥赛亚；能成为弥赛亚的是人之子，不可能是别人，只有对自然的不信才能期待另一个、一个超自然的弥赛亚；——超自然的东西只同自然之下的东西一起出现；因为整体虽然分离，却必须始终在场。——上帝就是爱，爱就是上帝，除了爱没有别的神性——只有不是神性的东西、不爱的东西，才不得不在观念中、在自己之外拥有神性。
谁不能相信上帝曾在耶稣之中、相信他住在人之中，谁就蔑视人。
如果爱住着，如果上帝住在人中间，那就可以有诸神；如果不是这样，那就只能谈论他，而诸神是不可能的；诸神只是各个分离的理想；如果一切都分离了，那就只有一个理想。

en: To destroy the objectivity of the commandments, of the laws, [means] to show that something is grounded in a need of man, in nature; to forgive sins (ἀφιέναι), to remit them, usually to sublate the punishments of sins — this [is] a miracle, for the effect cannot be separated from the cause, but above all fate cannot be annihilated; if one imagines a sublation of punishment, then punishment is something wholly objective, coming from something objective, not wholly necessarily connected with the guilt — in general, even if one takes punishment as something wholly inseparable from the guilt, it is still to that extent objective that it is the consequence of a law from which one has freed oneself in the transgression, but on which one still depends; with an objective law and judge the law is satisfied when I have been treated as I treated [others], when the separation that I made has likewise reacted back upon me, — in moral punishment the separated is not something external that I flee from, that I can overpower; the deed is the punishment in itself; as much as through the deed I have apparently injured foreign life, so much have I injured my own; life as life is not different from life; the injured life stands over against me as fate; it is satisfied when I have felt its power, — the power of the dead, just as in the crime I acted merely as power.

The law cannot be reconciled, for it always persists in its terrible majesty and cannot be gotten at by love; for it is hypothetical, and the possibility can never be sublated, the condition under which it enters can never become impossible; it rests as long as this condition does not enter, but is not sublated; but this rest is no reconciliation, because the law is indeed not something so persistent that it would have to be always effective and separate, but because it is conditioned, because it is possible only under [the condition of] a separation.

Fate, by contrast, can be reconciled, because it is itself one of the members, something separated, which cannot as something separated be annihilated by its opposite, but can be sublated through union.

Fate is the law itself that I have set up in the action (whether this be a transgression of another law or not), in its reaction back upon me; punishment is only the consequence of another law — the necessary consequence of something that has happened cannot be sublated, the action would have to be made undone; where there is nothing but causes and effects, as separated things, there no interruption of the series is possible.
Fate, by contrast, that is, the law itself reacting back, can be sublated; for a law that I myself have set up, a separation that I myself have made, I can also destroy.
Since action and reaction are one, it follows of itself that the reaction cannot be sublated one-sidedly.

Punishment is the consciousness of a foreign power, of something hostile; when it has worked itself out under the rule of the law, then this law is satisfied, and I am freed from something foreign that lets go of me and withdraws again into the threatening shape, but which I have not made into a friend.

The bad conscience is the consciousness of a bad action, of something that has happened, of a part of a whole over which I have no power; of something that has happened that can never, never be made undone, for it was something determinate, something limited.

Fate is the consciousness of itself (not of the action), of itself as a whole, this consciousness of the whole reflected, objectified; since this whole is a living thing that has injured itself, it can return again to its life, to love; its consciousness becomes again faith in itself, and the intuition of itself has become another, and fate is reconciled.

But love is then a need; in itself the rest is lost; this is the wound that remains, the intuition of itself as something actual; to which the intuition of itself as something striving, which removes itself from this actuality, is opposed; but because here there is only a striving, it is a need and is bound up with a melancholy that falls away only in love, the satisfied striving.
zh: 摧毁诫命、法则的客观性[意味着]表明，某样东西是建立在人的一种需要、建立在自然之上的；赦罪（ἀφιέναι），免除罪，通常就是扬弃对罪的惩罚——这是一桩奇迹，因为效果不能同原因分开，但尤其是命运不能被消灭；如果设想惩罚的扬弃，那么惩罚就是完全客观的东西，来自某个客观的东西，并不完全必然地与罪责相联系——总之，即使人们把惩罚看作与罪责完全不可分的东西，它也仍然是客观的，以至于它是一条法则的后果，人在违犯时摆脱了这条法则，却仍然依赖于它；在客观的法则和法官那里，法则得到满足，是在我受到我施加给别人的那种对待时，是在我所造成的分离同样反过来作用于我时——在道德的惩罚里，被分离出来的东西并不是我逃避的、我能制伏的一个外在物；行为本身就是惩罚；我在行为中表面上伤害了多少异己的生命，我就伤害了多少自己的生命；生命作为生命与生命没有区别；被伤害的生命作为命运与我相对而立；当我感受到了它的力量——死者的力量，它才得到满足，正如我在罪行中只是作为力量而行动一样。
法则无法得到和解，因为它始终固守在自己可怕的威严里，爱无法接近它；因为它是假设性的，那种可能性永远不能被扬弃，它出现所依据的条件永远不可能变得不可能；只要这个条件不出现，它就静止不动，但并没有被扬弃；可是这种静止并不是和解，因为法则虽然不是一种始终起作用、必须分离的持久东西，但它是被制约的，因为它只有在分离[的条件]下才可能。
命运却可以得到和解，因为它本身就是成员之一，是一种分离出来的东西，它作为分离出来的东西不能被自己的对立面消灭，却可以通过结合被扬弃。
命运就是我在行为中（无论这行为是不是对另一条法则的违犯）所设立的那条法则本身，在它对我的反作用中；惩罚只是另一条法则的后果——已经发生的事情的必然后果不能被扬弃，行为必须被弄得好像没有发生过；在只有原因和结果、只有分离的东西的地方，系列不可能被中断。
命运却可以被扬弃，也就是说，那条反作用的法则本身可以被扬弃；因为我自己设立的一条法则、我自己造成的一种分离，我也能够消灭。
既然行为和反作用是一回事，那就不言而喻，反作用不能单方面被扬弃。
惩罚是对一种外来力量、对一种敌对东西的意识；当它在法则的统治下发挥完作用，这条法则就得到满足，我也就从一种异己的东西中解脱出来，它放开了我，又缩回到那威胁性的形态里，但我并没有把它变成朋友。
恶的良知是对一个恶的行为的意识，是对一件已经发生的事情、对一个整体中我没有力量控制的部分的意识；是对一件已经发生的事情的意识，这件事永远、永远不能被弄成没有发生过，因为它曾经是确定的东西、有限的东西。
命运是对它自己（不是对行为）的意识，是对作为整体的它自己的意识，这种对整体的意识被反思、被对象化；既然这个整体是一个伤害了自己的活的东西，它就又能回到自己的生命、回到爱；它的意识又成为对自己的信仰，而它对自身的直观已经变成另一种，命运也就得到了和解。
但爱这时就是一种需要；静止在自身之中已经失去了；这就是留下来的伤口，是对自己作为现实东西的直观；而对自己作为一种努力、一种离开这种现实性的努力的直观，则与它相对立；但因为这里只有一种努力，所以它是需要，并且与一种忧伤相连，这种忧伤只在爱、在得到满足的努力中才消失。

en: Forgiveness of sins is therefore not the sublation of punishments (for every punishment is something positive, objective, that cannot be annihilated), not the sublation of the bad conscience, for no deed can become a non-deed; but fate reconciled through love.
Hence Jesus' rule: if you forgive the faults, your own are also forgiven you by the Father.
Forgiving others can only be the sublation of enmity, love that has returned, and this is whole; the forgiveness of faults comes out of it; this forgiveness is not a fragment, a single act.
Judge not, that you be not judged; do not set up any laws, for these hold for you too.
Jesus' confident expressions: Your sins are forgiven you, where he found faith and love, as with Mary Magdalene.

The authority that he gave his friends, to bind and to loose, when he had found in them the high faith in him (a human being); a faith that had felt the whole depth of human nature; this faith includes in itself the capacity to feel through others and to sense the harmony or disharmony of their being; to recognize their limits and their fate, - their bonds.

Return to morality does not sublate sins and their punishments, does not sublate fate; the deed remains; on the contrary, it only becomes all the more tormenting; the greater the morality, the more deeply the unmoral in it is felt, the punishment, fate is not sublated, because morality still always has an objective power standing over against it.
The sublation of the deed, compensation, is a wholly objective deed.
zh: 所以，罪的赦免不是对刑罚的扬弃（因为每一种刑罚都是某种肯定的、客观的东西，无法被消灭），不是对坏良心的扬弃，因为任何行为都不能变成非行为；而是通过爱而得到和解的命运。
所以有耶稣的那条规则：如果你们赦免过错，你们自己的过错也会被天父赦免。
能够宽恕别人的，只有对敌意的扬弃，即返回的爱，而爱是完整的；对过错的宽恕出自爱；这种宽恕不是一个碎片，不是一个单个的行为。
不要论断，免得你们被论断；你们不要立任何法律，因为这些法律对你们也有效。
耶稣那些有把握的说法：你的罪赦了——在他找到信仰和爱的地方，就像对抹大拉的马利亚那样。
他给朋友们的捆绑和释放的权柄，是他已经在他们身上找到了对他的（对一个人的）高度信仰时才给的；这种信仰感受过人性全部的深度；这种信仰自身包含着一种能力：透彻地体会别人，感到他们本质上的和谐或不和谐；认识他们的界限和他们的命运，——认识他们的束缚。
回到道德并不扬弃罪和罪的刑罚，也不扬弃命运；行为留了下来；恰恰相反，它只会变得更折磨人；道德越大，道德中不道德的东西就被感受得越深切，刑罚、命运并没有被扬弃，因为道德始终还有一种客观的力量与它相对而立。
对行为的扬弃，即赔偿，是一个完全客观的行为。

en: Joh.
5, 26 f.: the former [sc. the Father] the unique, undivided - the beautiful; this [sc. the Son] the modified - υἱὸς ἀνϑϱώπου, gone forth out of the unity.
Therefore he has power - against something hostile, standing over against him -, to hold judgment, a law against those who are apostate from him - kingdom of freedom and actuality.
zh: Joh.
5, 26 f.：前者〔即父〕是那唯一的、未分割的——美；这个〔即子〕是被改变者——υἱὸς ἀνϑϱώπου，从这种统一中走出来的。
因此他有权柄——针对某种敌对的、与他对立的东西——〔来〕施行审判，一条针对那些背离他的人的法则——自由和现实性的国度。

en: A. Ceremon[ies].
Commandments about holy things and service.
Against the privileges of the Jews Matth.
zh: A. 仪式〔Zeremonien〕。
关于神圣事物与侍奉的诫命。
针对犹太人的特权 Matth.

en: Fasting, Matth.

9, 14: human life and love exalted above it: V. 16-17: the incompatibility of the old with the new; the danger that threatens the self-determination of morality from the positive - fasting must depend on the mood of the mind, on joy or sorrow.
zh: 禁食，Matth.
9, 14：人的生命和爱高于它：V. 16-17：旧东西与新东西不能相容；实证的东西给道德的自我规定带来的危险——禁食必须取决于内心的情绪是喜还是悲。

en: Matth.
12, 1-8: desecration of the Sabbath - set over against it the example of their priests (the non-necessity) and the legislation of man; V. 11-12: the precedence of man's need.
zh: Matth.
12, 1-8：亵渎安息日——与之相对的是他们祭司的例子（不必要性）以及人的立法；V. 11-12：人的需要的优先。

en: 15, 2: washing hands before eating bread - set over against the Pharisees the transgressing of a commandment by the Pharisees themselves, through their objective commandments; V. 11, 20: for the rest of the people the disposition, the subjective in man, nothing objective is pure, no given purity.
zh: 15, 2：吃饼前洗手——与法利赛人相对的是法利赛人自己、通过他们那些客观的诫命对一条诫命的违犯；V. 11, 20：对其余的百姓来说则是意向，是人身上主观的东西，没有什么客观的东西是洁净的，没有给定的洁净。

en: 17, 25: tax - the king takes it only from strangers; thus the sons are free; but that they do not take offense (σϰανδαλίζειν).
zh: 17, 25：税——国王只向陌生人收；这样儿子们就是自由的；但他们不要因此反感（σϰανδαλίζειν）。

en: 19, 1: love, the disposition above the law - with regard to marriage.
zh: 19, 1：爱、意向高于法律——就婚姻而言。

en: 24. Kap.
zh: 24. Kap.

en: [B. Morality.]

Morality preserves, secures only the possibility of love and is therefore, as to its mode of acting, only negative; its principle is universality, i.e. to treat all as one's equals - as equal, the condition of love; the faculty of universality is reason; - a thoroughly merely moral human being is a miser, who always scrapes together and keeps means, without ever enjoying, - the moral act is always a limited one, because it is an act, and the disposition is one-sided and incomplete, because it is opposed to the act.
In morality without love, to be sure, the opposition to the single object is sublated in universality - a synthesis of objective [elements]; but the single is present as something excluded, opposed.
zh: [B. 道德]
道德只保持、只确保爱的可能性，所以按它的行为方式来说只是否定的；它的原则是普遍性，也就是把所有人都当作与自己同等的人——当作平等的来对待，这是爱的条件；普遍性的能力是理性；——一个完全只是道德的人是个守财奴，总是把手段聚拢起来、保存起来，从来不去享用，——道德的行为总是一个有限的行为，因为它是一个行为，而意向是片面的、不完整的，因为它与行为相对立。
在无爱的道德那里，普遍性中确实扬弃了对单个对象的对立——一种客观东西的综合；但单个的东西是作为被排除的、对立的东西而存在的。

en: Immorality cancels the possibility of love, through the maltreatment of living beings.

Return to morality through the reaction of the law, through fate and punishment, is fear of the objective, of that which one has maltreated, and that one is then also maltreated; return to legality, i.e. to the objective rule; to morality only through love, whose need [one] has felt for oneself, has made its satisfaction impossible for oneself through immorality, and respects the living.
zh: 不道德取消爱的可能性，通过虐待有生命的东西。
通过法律的反弹作用、通过命运和惩罚回到道德，是对客观东西的恐惧，是对自己虐待过的东西的恐惧，也是对自己随后同样会受虐待的恐惧；回到合法性，也就是回到客观的规则；只有通过爱才能回到道德，人已经自为地感受到对爱的需要，却通过不道德使自己对爱的满足成为不可能，并且尊重有生命的东西。

en: C. [Religion.]

The divinity — the more infinite the object, the more infinite the passivity; through morality and love this is lessened, but not brought to completed self-sufficiency — this [passivity] persists through struggle against the objective, and in this way no religion is possible.
Not to destroy the object but to reconcile it.
The law as ruling is sublated through virtue.
The limitation of virtue through love — but love itself feeling, with it reflection not united.
zh: C. 〔宗教。〕
神性——对象越是无限，受动性也越是无限；通过道德和爱，这种受动性被减少了，但没有被带到完全的独立性——这种〔受动性〕靠与客观东西的斗争而存在，而这样就不可能有宗教。
不是消灭对象，而是与对象和解。
作为统治者的法律通过美德被扬弃。
美德通过爱而受到限制——但爱本身是感受，反思没有与它结合在一起。

en: Love the blossom of life; the kingdom of God the whole tree with all necessary modifications, stages of development; the modifications are exclusions, not oppositions, i.e. there are no laws, i.e. the thought is equal to the actual, there is no universal, no relation has objectively become a rule, all relations have arisen livingly out of the development of life, no object is bound to an object, nothing has become fixed.
No freedom of opposition, no free I, no free thou.
Out of opposition through freedom rights arise.
Freedom without opposition is only a possibility.

Human beings are as they ought to be; the being-that-ought-to-be must of course then be an infinite striving, if the object is simply not to be overcome, if sensibility and reason — or freedom and nature, or subject and object — are so absolutely opposed that they are absoluta.
Through the syntheses: no object — no subject, or no I — no not-I, their character as absoluta is not cancelled.
zh: 爱是生命的花朵；上帝之国是整棵树，带着一切必要的变形、发展的阶段；这些变形是排除，不是对立，也就是说没有法律，也就是说被思考的东西与现实的东西相等，没有普遍的东西，没有任何关系客观地变成了规则，一切关系都是活生生地从生命的发展中产生出来的，没有一个对象被绑在另一个对象上，没有什么固定下来。
没有对立的自由，没有自由的我，没有自由的你。
从通过自由而来的对立中产生出权利。
没有对立的自由只是一种可能性。
人就是他们应该成为的样子；这种应当存在当然必须是一种无限的追求，如果对象根本就不可克服，如果感性和理性——或者自由和自然，或者主体和客体——如此绝对地对立，以致它们是 absoluta。
通过那些综合：没有客体——没有主体，或者没有我——没有非我，它们作为 absoluta 的性质并没有被扬弃。

en: Law is a thought relation of objects to one another; in the kingdom of God there can be no thought relation, because there are no objects for one another.
A thought relation is fixed and lasting, without spirit, a yoke, a chaining together, a lordship and bondage — activity and suffering — determining and being determined.
zh: 法律是诸对象彼此之间的一种被思考的关系，在上帝之国里不可能有被思考的关系，因为那里没有互为对象的对象。
一种被思考的关系是固定而持久的，没有精神，是一副枷锁，是一条锁链，是一种统治和奴役——能动和受动——规定和被规定。

en: Matth.

4, 17: μετανοει ͂τε ἤγγιϰεν γὰϱ ἡ βασιλεία τω ͂ν οὐϱανω ͂ν. — This is the first call and assurance that the kingdom of heaven is there — and the consequence of his call and his cures [are] many followers.
zh: Matth.
4, 17：μετανοει ͂τε ἤγγιϰεν γὰϱ ἡ βασιλεία τω ͂ν οὐϱανω ͂ν。——这是第一次呼召和保证，说上帝之国已经在此——而他的呼召和他的治病的后果〔是〕许多追随者。

en: Matth.
5, 17: πληϱω ͂σαι, to complete, to make full through the disposition, through adding the inner to the outer.
V. 20: the righteousness of his disciples must be more than that of the Pharisees and those who understand the law, there must besides this also be added that the law they follow is their own.

Another standard [is] set in opposition, the disposition, and by this passionate actions that change nothing in the subsistence of another [are] condemned just as much as the disturbance of his life existing for itself, and as the principle a readiness to reconcile, i.e. an inclination to cancel the separation, is given.
zh: Matth.
5, 17：πληϱω ͂σαι，补足，通过意向使之完全，也就是把内在的东西加到外在的东西上。
V. 20：他的门徒的正直必须多过法利赛人和懂法律的人的正直，除此之外还必须加上一点，即他们遵循的法律是他们自己的。
另一个尺度〔被〕对立地提出来，就是意向；按照这个尺度，那些并不改变别人的持续存在的激烈行动，受到的谴责与扰乱别人自为地持续着的生命一样，而作为原则给出的是和解意愿，也就是取消分离的倾向。

en: V. 21-22: to the objective prohibition of murder the disapproval of anger against one's brother is added, to the atoning sacrifice real reconciliation, etc. V. 33: to the [rule] that one should not swear falsely, that the oath should be kept to the Lord, [is added:] not to swear at all by something alien, not by heaven, for it is only the throne of God, etc., not by our hair, which is not wholly in our power, by nothing alien at all, to hang nothing on this, but to be ourselves; but if man is only one with himself, disdains every dependence, every covenant with the objects, he must nevertheless make a covenant with distress.
6, 25 ff.: Be unconcerned about distress.
zh: V. 21-22：在禁止杀人的客观禁令之外，加上了对向自己兄弟发怒的不满；在和解祭之外，加上了现实的和解，等等。V. 33：对于不可起假誓、要对主守誓这一条，〔又加上了：〕根本不要指着任何外在的东西起誓，不要指着天起誓，因为它只是上帝的宝座，等等；不要指着我们的头发起誓，因为它并不完全在我们的支配之下；总之不要指着任何外在的东西起誓，不要把什么挂在这上面，而是要成为我们自己；但人即使只与自己为一，蔑视一切依赖、一切与对象的结盟，他也还是必须与困境结盟。
6, 25 ff.：不要为困境忧虑。

en: With one's own bondage, the lordship that one exercises over others through the idea of the moral commandments also ceases.

7, 1 ff.: one's own freedom likewise grants others freedom — moral judging is death, recognizes nothing as existing for itself, [sees] everything only standing under one law, under one lordship, does not [see] essence and law as one, in one nature.
The principle of your relation to others is to honor their freedom and, what you therefore want from them, only to ask for it.
zh: 随着自己受奴役，人通过道德诫命的观念对别人行使的统治也随之停止。
7, 1 ff.：自己的自由也同样承认别人的自由——道德审判是死亡，它不承认任何自为地持续存在的东西，只把一切都看作处在一条法律之下、处在一种统治之下，不把本质和法律看作一，看作处在同一种自然里。
你们对别人的关系的原则，就是尊重他们的自由，并且，你们因此想从他们那里得到什么，就只能去请求。

en: Jesus, as the founder of a new religion among a corrupt people, characterized the renunciation of the comforts of life, and the same demand of it upon his helpers — also the tearing [out] of other relations and holy connections of life.
zh: 耶稣作为一个败坏民族中新宗教的创立者，所刻画的就是对生活舒适的弃绝，以及对他的助手们提出的同样要求——还有把人从生活其余的关系和神圣的联系中拽出来。

en: Matt.
8, 22: the answer he gave to his disciple who wanted to bury his father.
zh: 《马太福音》
8, 22：他给那个想埋葬自己父亲的弟子所作的回答。

en: Matt.
8, 10: the first statement about coldness among the Jews and their rejection.
zh: 《马太福音》
8, 10：关于犹太人那里的冷淡以及他们被弃绝的第一次说法。

en: 9, 15: fasting not for a purpose, but according to circumstances.
zh: 9, 15：禁食不是为了一个目的，而是看情况。

en: 9, 63, 10, 1 ff.: sending of the apostles into the country, not to reconcile men and to make the human race into friends — (Mark.
6, 7 Jesus sends them away, 6, 30 they gather themselves again to him; Luke.
9, 6 and 9, 10 back.
The universality of his reformation given up. — Matt.
10, 21 ff. a brother against the brother, the father [will] give the child over to death, children [will give] the parents [over to death].

V. 34: I came not to cast peace upon the earth, but the sword; I came to set the man against his father, the daughter against the mother, the bride against the mother-in-law at odds; the members of the household will be the enemies of the man; whoever loves father or mother, son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
Terrible tearing apart of all bonds of nature, the destruction of all nature. —
zh: 9, 63, 10, 1 及以下：把使徒派到乡间去，不是去使人彼此和解、使人类成为朋友——（《马可福音》
6, 7 耶稣把他们打发走，6, 30 他们又重新聚集到他那里；《路加福音》
他的改革的普遍性被放弃了。——《马太福音》
10, 21 及以下：兄弟反对兄弟，父亲[会]把孩子交出处死，孩子[会]把父母交出处死。
第 34 节：我来不是要把和平丢到地上，而是要把刀剑丢到地上；我来是要让男人与他的父亲对立，让女儿与她的母亲对立，让新娘与婆婆对立；家里的人会成为这男人的仇敌；谁爱父亲或母亲、儿子或女儿胜过爱我，就不配属于我。
对自然一切纽带的可怖撕裂，对一切自然的摧毁。——

en: Rising embitterment against his time Matt.
V. 25: you have hidden this from the understanding and the clever and revealed it to the simple; so was your good pleasure.
zh: 对他那个时代日益增长的怨愤，《马太福音》
第 25 节：你把这事向聪明通达人隐藏起来，向单纯的人显明出来；这就是你所乐意的。

en: 12, 8 ff.: the human being higher than the Sabbath.
zh: 12, 8 及以下：人比安息日更高。

en: V. 16: he forbade the healed man to say this.
zh: 第 16 节：他不许被治好的人说出这事。

en: V. 31: sin against the Son of Man indeed forgiven, but not the sin against the Holy Spirit.
zh: 第 31 节：对人之子的罪倒可以赦免，对神圣的精神的罪却不行。

en: V. 48: who is my mother and my brothers?
These, while he turned to his followers.
zh: 第 48 节：谁是我的母亲，谁是我的兄弟？
这些[人]——他说这话时转向了自己的追随者。

en: 13, 54-55: is this not the son of the carpenter?

Unbelief in human nature, contempt for all human relations — hence his removal from them, in the opinion that they were not sanctified; a prophet counts for nothing in his fatherland; on this see above 10, 36 ff.
Purity defiled by everything, not to be restored, fate cannot be escaped when beauty has fled out of everything; so he gave up everything in order to restore it alone first.
zh: 13, 54-55：这不是木匠的儿子吗？
对人性不信，对一切人的关系蔑视——因此他远离这些关系，因为他认为它们没有被神圣化；先知在本乡不算什么；关于这一点参见前面 10, 36 及以下。
纯洁被一切东西玷污了，无法再恢复，当美从一切东西里逃走之后，命运是逃不掉的；于是他放弃了一切，只为了先把它单独恢复起来。

en: 15, 2: the Pharisees again hold up a positive commandment to him, his answer as in the Sermon on the Mount.
zh: 15, 2：法利赛人又拿一条实证的诫命来责问他，他的回答和在登山宝训里一样。

en: 16, 16-17: you are Christ, the Son of the living God - my Father has revealed it to you, not flesh and blood; v. 19: I give you the keys of the kingdom of God - what you bind on earth shall be bound in heaven, etc.
zh: 16, 16-17：你是基督，是永生上帝的儿子——是我父把它启示给你的，不是血肉；第 19 节：我把上帝之国的钥匙给你——你在世上所捆绑的，在天上也要捆绑，等等。

en: [Ch.] 18: if you do not become like the children.
v. 20: if two of you are of one mind about something, it will be granted to you by my Father.
v. 21 ff.: forgiveness of faults.
18, 18: indeed to loose; binding and loosing, giving laws - as soon as Peter had shown faith in Jesus as Messiah, he shows himself free of the objective and filled with the greatness of human nature.
zh: ［第］18 章：你们若不变成小孩子那样。
第 20 节：你们中间若有两个人对某件事同心，我父就会把它赐给你们。
第 21 节及以下：饶恕过错。
18, 18：确实能解开；捆绑和解开，颁布法律——彼得一显出对耶稣作为弥赛亚的信仰，就显出自己摆脱了客观的东西，充满人性之伟大。

en: 19, 8: marriage exalted above civil legislation.
zh: 19, 8：婚姻高居于市民立法之上。

en: 19, 12: only he who can may follow this rule.
zh: 19, 12：只有做得到的人，才可以照这条规则做。

en: 19, 20: the request of Zebedee's wife for her sons.
zh: 19, 20：西庇太的妻子为她的儿子们提出的请求。

en: 25, 40: what you have done to one of the least, you have done to me.
zh: 25, 40：你们做在这最小的一个人身上的，就是做在我身上。

en: 26, 7: the woman who poured fragrant water over him - his followers [demanded] morality according to purposes and censured the free beautiful outpouring of a loving soul.
zh: 26, 7：那个女人把芬芳的水浇在他身上——他的追随者［要求］合乎目的的道德，并责备一个爱的灵魂自由而美好的流露。

en: v. 10: ϰαλὸν ἔϱγον, a beautiful deed - the only deed in the history of the Jews that deserves the epithet ϰαλόν, also the only beautiful deed that happens (26, 24: ϰαλὸν ἠ ͂ν αὐτω ͂ͅ, that he had not been born, ϰαλόν is more a meaningless phrase).
zh: 第 10 节：ϰαλὸν ἔϱγον，一件美好的行为——犹太人历史上唯一配得上 ϰαλόν 这个称号的行为，也是唯一在发生的美好行为（26, 24：ϰαλὸν ἠ ͂ν αὐτω ͂ͅ，即他还不如没有出生，ϰαλόν 在那里更是一句没有意义的话）。

en: Mark.

16, 17: signs that will accompany the believers, supernatural powers, what nature was capable of was present, was there as appearance, as deed; it had happened - all sides of human nature had become custom, habit, way of life of the peoples, objective; deeds that as deeds were to be divine had to be supernatural - for nothing that happens is divine, but what is.
Something divine that happens is greater than what others do, therefore relative.

The deed in itself is the connection of the successive objective; as much suffering in the one, so much activity in the other, and every objective is a universal, precisely because it stands under a law.
zh: 《马可福音》
16, 17：伴随信徒的记号，超自然的力量——自然所能做到的，已经存在，已经作为现象、作为行动在那里；它已经发生了——人类本性的所有方面都已经成为各民族的习俗、习惯、生活方式，成为客观的；作为行动而应当是神圣的行动，必须是超自然的——因为凡是发生的东西都不是神圣的，神圣的是存在的东西。
某种发生的神圣东西，比别人所做的更大，因此是相对的。
行动就其自在来说，是前后相继的客观东西的关联；一个里面有多少受动，另一个里面就有多少能动，而每一个客观的东西都是普遍的东西，正因为它处在一条法律之下。

en: Jesus began his preaching by proclaiming that the kingdom of God is there; the Jews expected the return of the theocracy; they were to believe it, and the kingdom of God can be there in faith; what is present in faith is opposed to actuality and to the concept of it.
The universal expresses an ought, because it is a thought, because it is not, for the same reason why determinate being cannot be proved.
zh: 耶稣开始布道时宣告说，上帝之国就在眼前；犹太人期待的是神权政治的复归；他们应当相信这一点，而上帝之国可以在信仰中就在眼前；在信仰中存在的东西，与现实性和关于现实性的概念相对立。
普遍的东西表达一个应当，因为它是被思想的东西，因为它并不存在，出于同一条理由，定在也无法被证明。

en: The kingdom of God is the condition when the deity rules, thus when all determinations and all rights are sublated; hence to the young man: sell what is yours - it is hard for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God -, hence Christ's renunciation of all property and all honour; these relations to father, family, property could not become beautiful relations, so they were not to be there at all, so that at least the opposite would not be there - either through a leap or through the successive sublation of the individual determinations through dissolution; the former Jesus attempted through enthusiasm, he assured that the kingdom of God is there, to pronounce the determinate being of a thing.
zh: 上帝之国就是神性统治时的状态，也就是一切规定和一切权利都被扬弃的状态；所以他对那个青年说：把你所有的卖掉——财主进上帝之国是难的——，所以基督放弃一切财产和一切荣誉；这些对父亲、家庭、财产的关系不可能变成美好的关系，所以它们根本就不该在那里，好让至少相反的东西不在那里——要么通过一次跳跃，要么通过分解来逐个扬弃各个规定；前一条路耶稣用热情去尝试，他保证上帝之国就在眼前，就是说出一个东西的定在。

en: The Jews expected with the kingdom of God that much would happen, that they would be freed from the rule of the Romans, that their priesthood would be restored in its old splendour, etc., that is, that outside them many changes would take place; such Jews could not believe that the kingdom of God is there when Jesus proclaimed it to them; but those who rested in themselves, who were completed, could believe it; not as isolated ones, for God is in nothing isolated, but in living community, which, considered in the individual, is faith in humanity, faith in the kingdom of God - faith is the individual over against the living - not that God's laws rule, for God and his laws are not two things.
zh: 犹太人和上帝之国一起期待的，是许多事情会发生，是他们从罗马人的统治下被解放出来，是他们的祭司制度恢复旧日的光彩，等等，也就是说，在他们之外会发生许多变化；这样的犹太人无法相信，当耶稣向他们宣告它的时候，上帝之国就在眼前；而那些立足于自身、已经完成的人，却能相信它；不是作为孤立的人，因为上帝不在任何孤立的东西里面，而在活的共同体里面，这共同体在个人身上来看，就是对人性的信仰，对上帝之国的信仰——信仰是与活的东西相对的个别的东西——不是上帝的法律在统治，因为上帝和他的法律不是两回事。

en: Life and return to life, but no rule about it in Luke.
zh: 生命和回到生命，但《路加福音》里没有关于此事的规则。

en: 98) B. Morality.
Sermon on the Mount, Matt.
Jesus begins with crying out, in that before the assembled crowd he gives vent to his heart, to his other way of judging human worth.

Enthusiastically [he] cries it out that it is now a matter of another righteousness, of another worth of human beings, enthusiastically he at once removes himself from the common estimation of the virtues and announces another region of life, in which one of its joys must be to be persecuted by the world, to which they must show their opposition.
But the new life is not to break the matter of the laws, but rather to be their fulfilment, the completion of what has hitherto been present under the form of an opposite, as law.
This form of being commanded is to be destroyed by its new life and to vanish before the fullness of its spirit, of its essence.
zh: 登山宝训，《马太福音》
耶稣以呼喊开始，他在聚集起来的人群面前把自己的心、把自己评判人的价值的另一种方式一吐为快。
他满怀热情地喊出来：现在关系的是另一种正义，是人的另一种价值；他满怀热情地立刻离开对诸美德的庸常评价，宣告另一个生命领域，在这个领域里，被世界迫害必定是它的快乐之一，而他们必须向世界表明自己对它的对立。
但新生命不要打碎法律的质料，它反倒是法律的完成，是对迄今以对立物的形式、作为法律而存在的东西的补充。
这种被命令的形式应当由它新的生命来消灭，并在它的精神、它的本质的充实面前消失。

en: V. 21-26: The law against killing is fulfilled by the higher genius of conciliatoriness and at the same time sublated for it; for it there is no such commandment.
zh: 第 21-26 节：禁止杀人的法律，被更高的和解天才所履行，同时又被它扬弃；对它来说，并没有这样的诫命。

en: V. 27-30: The higher law against adultery is fulfilled by the holiness of love and by the capacity, when one of the many sides of the human being engages itself, to raise itself to its wholeness.
zh: 第 27-30 节：禁止通奸的更高法律，通过爱的神圣性、也通过这样一种能力得到履行：当人身上许多方面中的一个方面参与进来时，能把自己提升到自己的整体。

en: V. 31-32: Divorce; the sublation of love, of his friendship toward a woman, in which she still is, makes her become unfaithful to herself and sin, and the observance of legal duties and decency is a wretched whitewash, a new harshness in this violation of her love.
zh: 第 31-32 节：离婚；扬弃爱，扬弃他对一个女人的友谊——而她还在这友谊里——就使她对自己不忠、使她犯罪，而遵守法定的义务和体面，是一种可怜的美化，是在这样伤害她的爱时又添上的新的冷酷。

en: V. 33-37: if you are truthful, then you need not tie the connection between your speech and the deed or thought to something foreign, lay it into the hand of a foreigner, declare him the lord of this connection — you yourself are exalted above all foreign power.
The law not to swear falsely, but to make God into the power over one's word, is fulfilled by truthfulness, and at the same time truthfulness is exalted above it.
zh: 第 33-37 节：你若真诚，就不必把你的话与行动或思想之间的联系系到一个异己的东西上，不必把它放到一个异己者的手里，不必宣布他是这种联系的主人——你自己就高于一切异己的力量。
不要起假誓、却把上帝立为自己话语之上的权力，这条法律由真诚得到履行，而同时真诚又高于它。

en: V. 38-42: justice — complete elevation above the sphere of right or wrong through the sublation of all property.
zh: 第 38-42 节：公正——通过扬弃一切财产，完全上升到权利或不义的领域之上。

en: V. 43 ff.: summary of the whole.
zh: 第 43 节及以下：对整体的概括。

en: 6, 1-4: alms not before people, not before yourself.
zh: 6, 1-4：施舍不在人前，也不在你自己面前。

en: V. 5-15: prayer; here too let only the praying be pure; mix in nothing foreign, being seen; but pray in your little chamber, and such a lonely and single prayer is the Our Father.
It is not the prayer of a people to its God, but the prayer of an isolated, insecure, uncertain one.

Thy kingdom come, thy name be hallowed; the wish of an individual — and a people cannot wish: thy will be done, a people of honour and pride does its own will and knows of no other than a hostile one — the individual can see the will of God and the universal as opposed.

Give us today our ... etc. — a petition of quiet simplicity, which would not fit in the mouth of a people that is conscious of its dominion over the means of nourishment or can impossibly have only the thought of the food of one day, but can well pray for the thriving of the whole, for a kindly nature; to pray is not to beg; forgive us — also a prayer of the individual; nations are separated, set-apart ones, it is not conceivable how they should forgive another nation; it could not happen through a union, but through the feeling of equality or of the preponderance of power, fear. — The consciousness of one's own sins, this reflection, it can obtain only through pain; for it cannot acknowledge its will under a law.
But the individual can pray: as much love as I have, so much may I experience.
zh: 第 5-15 节：祈祷；在这里也应当只有祷告是纯粹的；不要掺进任何异己的东西，不要掺进被人看见〔的念头〕；而是要在你的小屋里祷告，而这样一种孤独的、单个的祷告就是主祷文。
这不是一个民族向它的神的祈祷，而是一个孤立的、没有把握的、不确定的人的祈祷。
愿你的国降临，愿你的名被尊为圣；这是一个个人的愿望——而一个民族不能这样愿望：愿你的旨意成就，一个讲荣誉和骄傲的民族行的是自己的意志，除了一个敌对的意志，它不知道别的意志——个人却可以把上帝的意志和普遍的东西看成是对立的。

今天赐给我们我们的……等等——这是安静的单纯所发出的请求，它不会适合一个民族的嘴，这个民族意识到自己对食物的支配，或者不可能只想到一天的饭食，而是可以为整体的兴旺、为友好的自然祈祷；祈祷不是乞求；赦免我们——这也是个人的祈祷；民族是分离的、被隔开的，无法想象它们怎么会宽恕另一个民族；这不可能通过一种结合发生，而只能通过平等感或权力的优势感、通过恐惧发生。——对自己罪的认识，这种反思，一个民族只能通过痛苦获得；因为它无法承认自己的意志处在一条法律之下。
但个人可以祈祷：我有多少爱，就愿我体验到多少。

en: V. 16-18: fasting; as with praying and almsgiving, mix in nothing foreign.
zh: 第 16-18 节：禁食；像在祈祷和施舍时一样，不要掺进任何异己的东西。

en: V. 20-34: not to scatter oneself and not to lose the whole in cares and dependence; such partial things, needs, wealth, food, clothing bring a determinacy into the human being that makes him objectively incapable of pure life.
zh: 第 20-34 节：不要分散自己，不要在忧虑和依赖中丢掉整体；这些局部的物、需要、财富、食物、衣服，给人带来一种规定性，使他在客观上没有能力过纯粹的生命。

en: 7, 1-5: judging over others, subjecting them to a rule in the judgment, the tyranny in thoughts.
zh: 7, 1-5：论断别人，在判断中把他们置于一条规则之下，这是思想中的专制。

en: V. 7-12: the union of human beings in requesting and giving.
zh: 第 7-12 节：人在请求和给予中的结合。

en: V. 13 ff.: general image of the completed human being.
zh: 第 13 节及以下：完满的人的普遍图像。

en: Matt.

12, 31 f.: whoever blasphemes the human being blasphemes the single, the particular; but whoever blasphemes the Holy Spirit blasphemes nature and is incapable of attaining forgiveness of sins; for he is incapable of uniting himself with the whole; he remains isolated and excluded; such a sin comes out of the fullness of the heart and shows its destruction, its derangement; his unholiness is incapable of the holy that he has blasphemed; and the holy, considered according to separation and union, is love.
A sign might perhaps shake you — but the expelled spirit comes back with seven others, and the human being becomes more deranged than before.
zh: 《马太福音》
12, 31 及以下：谁亵渎人，亵渎的就是单个的东西、特殊的东西；谁亵渎神圣的精神，亵渎的就是自然，并且无法获得罪的赦免；因为他无法与整体结合；他仍然是孤立的、被排除在外的；这样一种罪出自内心的充实，显示出内心的毁坏、内心的紊乱；他的不神圣无法企及他所亵渎的那种神圣；而神圣，从分离和结合来看，就是爱。
一个征兆也许能震动你们——但被赶出去的精神带着另外七个回来，人就变得比先前更加紊乱。

en: On C. Religion.
zh: 关于 C. 宗教。

en: Matt.
18, 1-10: the greatest ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν [is] the one who comes closest to the children; their angels (V. 10) in heaven see continually the face of the Father who is in heaven.
By the angels of the children no objective beings can be understood, for also of the angels of other human beings (to speak in this tone) it would have to be thought that they behold God.

Their undeveloped unity, the unconscious, their being and life in God, represented in a shape; then this too is again substantialized, isolated, their relation to God an eternal beholding of the same.

In order to designate the spirit, the divine beyond the form of this limitation, and the community of this limited living creature, Plato puts pure life and the limited into a difference of time; he lets the pure spirits have lived before entirely in the beholding of the divine and be the same in earthly life, only with a darkened consciousness of that heavenly [realm].

In another way Jesus designates the nature, the divine, of the child-spirit as angels that always live in the beholding of God; also in this form they are represented not as God but as sons of God, as particular [beings].

The opposition of the beholding one to the beheld, that they are opposed, a subject and an object, drops away in the beholding itself — their difference is only the possibility of separation; a human being who always beheld the sun would be only a feeling of the light, the feeling as essence.
The one who lived entirely in the beholding of another human being would be this other himself, only with the possibility of being other.

Immediately connected with this is — for ὁ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ἦλθε σῶσαι τὸ ἀπολωλός [18, 11] — the commandment to reconcile oneself, to sublate disunion and to become one; this unity is the beholding of God, the becoming like children.
If the offender does not listen to the congregation, then let him be as a heathen and a tax collector; whoever separates himself, scorns the attempted union, holds firmly against it ...
zh: 《马太福音》
18, 1-10：ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν 中最大的〔那一个〕，就是离孩子最近的人；他们的天使（第 10 节）在天上常常看见那在天上的父的面。
在孩子的天使那里，不能理解成任何客观的存在者，因为就连别人的天使（如果要用这种调子说的话），也必然要设想成是在直观上帝。
他们那未展开的统一，那无意识的东西，他们在上帝中的存在和生命，被表象在一个形态里；然后这个形态又被实体化、被孤立，他们与上帝的关系成了对上帝的永恒直观。
为了标示精神，标示这种限制的形式之外的神性，以及这种受限的活物的共同体，柏拉图把纯粹的生命和受限的东西放进一种时间的差别里；他让那些纯粹的精灵先前完全生活在神性的直观之中，并且在尘世生命中还是同一个东西，只是对那属天之物的意识变暗了。
耶稣用另一种方式把孩子精神的本性、把它的神性标示为天使，这些天使永远生活在上帝的直观里；即使在这个形式里，他们也不是被表象为上帝，而是被表象为上帝的儿子、被表象为特殊者。
直观者与被直观者的对立，即它们是对立的、一个是主体、一个是客体，在直观本身中消失了——它们的区别只是分离的可能性；一个始终直观着太阳的人，就只是一种对光的感受，是把感受当作本质。
一个完全生活在另一个人的直观之中的人，就是这另一个人本身，只不过带着成为他者的可能性。
与此直接联系在一起的——因为 ὁ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ἦλθε σῶσαι τὸ ἀπολωλός［18, 11］——是那条诫命：与自己和解，扬弃分裂，成为一体；这种统一就是对上帝的直观，就是变得像孩子。
如果冒犯者不听教团的话，就让他像异教徒和税吏一样；谁把自己分隔出来，鄙弃那尝试过的结合，坚决地对抗它……

en: Further, V. 19: Jesus presents this oneness in another form: if two are at one about something and you ask for it, the Father will grant it to you.
The expressions to ask, to grant have become so common and are ...
zh: 此外，V. 19：耶稣用另一种形式来表述这种一致：如果两个人对某件事是一致的，而你们为此祈求，那么父就会把它赐给你们。
祈求、赐予这些说法已经变得如此平庸，并且会……

en: D. History - the form in which he as a single individual stands against single individuals and single individuals against him, the spread of his teaching.
zh: D. 历史——他作为单个的人与单个的人相对立、单个的人与他相对立的形式，他的学说的传播。

en: The beginning of his preaching.
Matth.
4, 17, ebd. 19: the winning of Simon and others.
zh: 他布道的开始。
Matth.
4, 17，ebd. 19：招募西门和其他人。

en: V. 22: in both cases the doing without the web of human relations and needs - separation from their life.
But not seclusion from tax collectors and sinners, Matth.
zh: V. 22：在两种情况下都是放弃人的关系和需要的织网——与他们的生命分离。
但不是与税吏和罪人隔绝，Matth.

en: Condition of the Jewish people, like sheep without shepherds: 9, 36.
zh: 犹太民族的状态，像没有牧人的羊群：9, 36。

en: To the Pharisees 16, 3: can you not judge the signs of the time?
zh: 对法利赛人说 16, 3：你们不能判断这时代的征兆吗？

en: Sending out of the twelve Matth.
Their instruction.

Sermon: ἤγγιϰεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐϱανῶν [the kingdom of God has drawn near, 10, 7] - everything else negative, do not care for travel needs; see where you find worthy people; if the house is worthy, let your greeting (εἰϱήνη, he had earlier commanded to greet a house) come upon it; if not, let it return to you yourselves - the greeting is in both cases the same, it depends on the worthiness of the house whether it resounds in it as word or whether the same fullness with which it is given strikes the minds in it; otherwise it returns to you; you have not squandered the peace, it is heard in you.
Thus no instructing and handling and drilling, hatred of the world, persecution; the spirit will speak out of you, do not be troubled about what you want to say.
Fearlessness, partly because of their own suffering, partly because of the disruption that their mission will bring upon the world.
zh: 差遣那十二人 Matth.
给他们的指示。

布道：ἤγγιϰεν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐϱανῶν〔上帝之国近了，10, 7〕——其余的一切都是否定的，不要为旅途的需要操心；看看你们在哪里找到配得上的人；如果那家是配得上的，你们的问候（εἰϱήνη，他先前吩咐过要问候一家人）就临到它；如果不是，就让它回到你们自己这里——问候在两种情况下都是同一个，关键在那家是否配得：它是作为话语在那家里回响，还是以给出它时同样的充盈击中那里的人心；否则它就回到你们那里；你们并没有浪费这平安，它在你们自己里面被听见。
所以不是教导、摆弄和操练，世界的仇恨、迫害；精神会从你们里面说话，不要为你们该说什么发愁。
无所畏惧，一部分是由于他们自己的受苦，一部分是由于他们的使命将给世界带来的动乱。

en: V. 41: whoever receives a prophet as a prophet (εἰς ὄνομα πϱοϕήτου), for whom a prophet is a prophet - a righteous man as righteous, a disciple as such, he has the reward, the value of a prophet; as a human being grasps a human being, so he himself is.
zh: V. 41：谁把一个先知当作先知来接纳（εἰς ὄνομα πϱοϕήτου），对谁来说一个先知就是一个先知——把一个义人当作义人，把一个门徒当作门徒，谁就得到那份报偿，即一个先知的价值；人怎样领会人，他自己就是怎样。

en: Displeasure at the way his teachings were received by his age (Matth.

Restriction of their efficacy to νηπίους, ϰοπιῶντας, πεϕοϱτισμένους [the immature, the weary, the laden]; from here begin his violent expressions against the Pharisees; his answers to questions and occasions aim only at silencing them, only polemical, the true he addresses to the other hearers.
zh: 对他的时代接受他的学说的方式的不满（Matth.
它们的效力被限制在 νηπίους, ϰοπιῶντας, πεϕοϱτισμένους〔婴孩、劳苦的人、负重的人〕身上；他从这里开始对法利赛人说出激烈的言辞；他对问题、由头的回答只是为了让他们闭嘴，只是论战性的，真的东西他是讲给别的听众的。

en: Matth.
12, 49: Jesus' separation from the relations of life.
zh: Matth.
12, 49：耶稣与生命诸关系的分离。

en: Parables Matth.

On the manner of the spread of his teaching, of the fate of the same, all (of the good sower, wheat and tares, mustard seed, leaven, found treasure, etc.) quite analogous to the myths - but to be sure Jewish ones, [attached] to actualities.

There is in them no fabula docet, no moral comes out of them, but the historical, the becoming, the progress of what is, of the eternal, of the living; - the becoming of being is the secret of nature; and all insipid chatter about a more inward conviction of the good etc. is infinitely more senseless than supernatural illumination, rebirth etc. The multitude of parables shows the inability to present that to which they are supposed to point. only that the precious thing is a great thing to be wished for, but a different one than they know.
V. 55: they see nothing but actuality, not the spirit, nothing but what they themselves are.
So too Matth.

These parables are neither Oriental allegories nor Greek myths; these two speak of the matter itself, of being, of the beautiful, whose development, going forth out of itself, changes among the Orientals mostly become such monstrous and unnatural births because they are held for themselves - by imagination alone, hence as monsters, [while] among the Greeks they indeed also appear as substances, as modifications in a living, actual [element], but are fastened by imagination to a natural action, to a human form; they do not thereby lose the ideal which the Oriental monsters want to keep for them; yet no individual life comes about (Ceres, Venus, etc.); the inhuman in these divine shapes is only liberation from what is heterogeneous to them, e.g. heaviness, work, need, etc. These parables of Christ are actual similes, modern fables, in which there is a tertium comparationis, i.e. where the same is thought (in the old Aesopian fables it was drives themselves, instincts, life modified in the same way), in the parables quite actual stories, hence always an even-as.
zh: 比喻 Matth.
关于他的学说传播的方式、这种学说的命运，所有这些（好撒种者、麦子和稗子、芥菜种、酵、找到的财宝等等）都与神话完全类似——但当然是犹太的神话，〔接在〕现实的诸事物上。
它们里面没有 fabula docet，从它们里面得不出什么道德教训，得出的是历史性的东西、生成，是存在者、永恒者、活生生者的进程；——存在的生成是自然的秘密；而一切关于对善有更内在的确信之类的乏味空谈，比起超自然的启示、重生等等来要无限地更没意义。比喻的数量之多显示出无力把比喻所指向的东西表述出来。只是那珍贵的东西是一种大可欲求的东西，但却是与他们所知不同的另一种东西。
V. 55：他们除了现实性什么都看不见，看不见精神，只看得见他们自己所是的东西。
Matth. 也是这样。

这些比喻既不是东方的寓意，也不是希腊的神话；这两者讲的是事情本身，讲的是存在，讲的是美——美的展开、从自身走出、变化，在东方人那里大多变成极其庞大而不自然的产儿，因为它们被自为地——单由想象力、于是当作怪物——把持着，〔而〕在希腊人那里虽然也作为实体、作为一个活生生的、现实的东西中的变形出现，但毕竟被想象力拴在一种自然的行动上、拴在一种人的形象上；它们并不因此失去那种理想的东西，而东方的怪物却想为它们保住这种东西；可毕竟没有产生出个体生命（刻瑞斯、维纳斯等等）；这些神的形象身上不合人性的地方，只是对与它们相异的东西的摆脱，例如重力、劳作、困厄等等。基督的这些比喻是真正的比喻，是现代的寓言，其中有一个比较的第三项，也就是说，那里思考的是相同的东西（在古老的伊索寓言里，那本身就是冲动、本能，是同样被改变了的生命），在比喻里则是完全现实的故事，所以总是一个“正如”。
